entries.claim: The entry cap is only applied after an unbounded `git log` result has been collected, so the default `--top 10` does not actually bound resource consumption and can fail on a file with a large history.
entries.failure_scenario: A repository has a frequently modified file with enough commit subjects/history to make `git log --format=... --follow` exceed Node's `execFileSync` default stdout `maxBuffer` (about 1 MiB). `bareArgv` has no git-side `-n` limit, so `runGit` throws before `renderChain` can slice to 10 entries; it is converted to status 1 and the user receives `git-failed` instead of the requested capped chain. Even below that threshold, all history is unnecessarily held in memory for a response intended to be capped.

counter_evidence.note: Measured on this repository: the largest per-file `git log --format=<LOG_FORMAT>` output is ~57 KB (401 commits on .planning/STATE.md), and 144 commits on planning.mjs yields 20,377 bytes. Reaching the 1 MiB execFileSync default needs roughly 7,000 commits touching one path. The claim is factually correct - no maxBuffer is passed at why.mjs:48 and renderChain slices at why-render.mjs:116, after collection - but the failure is a clean `git-failed` envelope rather than a crash or a wrong answer, and it is unreachable on the corpus this seam was built to read. Severity medium overstated; ruled low and queued as an open item.

entries.claim: Commit subjects are emitted verbatim into the skill's terminal-facing `text` without neutralizing terminal control characters.
entries.failure_scenario: An untrusted contributor creates a commit whose subject contains ESC control bytes, for example an OSC-8 hyperlink or OSC-52 clipboard sequence. Git returns that subject through `%s`; `renderEntry` incorporates it directly, and `cad-why` parses the JSON then prints `text` verbatim. The caller's terminal can therefore render attacker-controlled links or process terminal escape sequences merely from querying a file's history.

counter_evidence.note: The claim is correct: renderEntry at why-render.mjs:89-98 interpolates %s verbatim and nothing in why-query.mjs, why-render.mjs or why.mjs neutralizes control bytes. Ruled low rather than medium: the seam RELAYS git output rather than parsing untrusted input unsafely, `git log` itself emits the same bytes to the same terminal by default, and the precondition is an attacker who already authors commits in the queried history. No Cadence lib sanitizes control characters today, so this is a new hardening class rather than a regression in this diff. Queued as an open item.
